content.title: How to watch Rockets vs Lakers playoff Game 1: Time, TV, live stream
content.text: The Rockets face the Lakers in playoff Game 1 as Houston opens its first-round series on the road.Billy CaddenThe Houston Rockets are back in the playoffs and open their first-round series Saturday night against the Lakers in Los Angeles. Houston finished the season strong at 52-30, earning the No. 5 seed and missing out on home court by just one game behind the 53-29 Lakers. That puts the Rockets on the road to start the series, but they come in with plenty of momentum after closing the regular season on a 9-1 run. Now, they’ll look to carry that form into a matchup that oddsmakers believe leans heavily in their favor despite the seeding.While the Lakers still have LeBron James, they’ll be shorthanded early in the series with Luka Dončić and Austin Reaves both sidelined, giving Houston a major opportunity to strike first. Kevin Durant will make his playoff debut for the Rockets, and alongside Alperen Şengün, Houston has the more complete roster heading into this series. The odds reflect that, with the Rockets entering Game 1 as 5.5-point favorites on the road. Stealing the opener in Los Angeles would be a massive statement and could set the tone for the entire series, making Saturday night’s game as important as it gets.Saturday’s game tips off at 7:30 p.m. CST, and Rockets fans across the country can tune in with Sling TV.When is the Rockets vs Lakers playoff Game 1? What: Houston Rockets @ Los Angeles Lakers — First Round Game 1 When: Saturday, April 18, 2026, at 7:30 p.m. CST Where: Crypto.com Arena, Los Angeles, CA TV: ABC How to stream the Rockets vs Lakers Game 1 without cableBeing Game 1 of arguably the most star-studded series in the first round, it’s no surprise that Saturday’s game will be broadcast across the country on ABC. This makes it super easy to tune in without cable TV, as you can even pick up an antenna on Amazon and tune in to your local ABC station. But if you want to make sure you can catch as many Rockets games as possible, you should consider signing up for a streaming service with live TV, and we always recommend Sling TV.With the Sling Select package carrying ABC in most markets — including here in Houston — its $24.99/month subscription is among the most affordable. That said, you may want to upgrade to a Sling Orange & Blue plan for $64.99/month since that’s the only way to get ABC, NBC, and ESPN from Sling, which is where you’ll find the majority of the playoff games this postseason. These are all the ways to tune in Saturday night with Sling: Sling TV 3-Month Prepay ($49.99 - $159.99 then monthly recurring payments) Sling TV Select ($24.99/month) Sling TV Blue ($49.99/month) Sling TV Orange & Blue ($64.99/month) If you don’t want to sign up for Sling, you can go with any of the other streaming options below and still catch the game: fuboTV ($48.99 for the first month, then $73.99/month with a 7-day free trial) DIRECTV STREAM ($89.99/month; no free trials available at this time) Hulu + Live TV ($89.99/month with a 3-day free trial; also includes Disney+ and ESPN+) YouTube TV ($67.99/month for the first three months, then $82.99/month with a 5-day free trial) It’s worth noting that some of the Rockets’ early postseason games will air on Amazon Prime Video (including Game 3 of this series), so you’ll need to sign up for that as well to catch all the playoff action.April 18, 2026Andrew Koopman is a freelance writer who's been producing content since 2020. If he's not writing, Andrew is almost certainly watching sports (go Warriors!) or planning his next adventure as he attempts to visit all 50 states in the next few years.
